added.summary: A flow segment can be live: a timeline with a `scene` track (and a `camera` or `shot` track) instead of footage, or footage over a scene. A playable segment stops at its `flow.hold` marker until the game calls og.flow.advance(world, flow, outcome), which takes the node's hidden `#outcome:<name>` choice; a choice the player takes while it holds cuts at once. og.Flow.held, FlowView.held and WindowView.held say it holds. The cook checks outcomes (one word, named once, only on a held segment, never with #default, #qte or #hotspot) (flow §3).

og.flow.advance(world, flow, outcome?) ends the segment playing now: by the named #outcome, else the window's choice or the default. What a level or minigame between segments calls when it is won or lost.
A camera track takes `blendIn` and `blendOut` seconds: it eases from the camera it took at the timeline's start, and back to it before its end, cubic in and out (animation §13).

fixed.summary: Every flow cut calls og.render.snapCamera, so a segment's camera never blends from the last one's; and when one deck's timeline lets go of og.Camera as another takes it in the same tick, the new one takes the camera the old one handed back, whatever order the decks run in.
